body: I thought this was an error we didn't catch in `backend.IsNotFound`. However I can't find any error in the goleveldb repo named "key not found".
We leak a potential `backend.errNotFound` in `fillBlockList` if the block list is missing. That's not supposed to happen, of course...
Nonetheless it does, and somewhat frequently too. I've pulled the release for now...

We can avoid the panic by returning a not-found for the entire file entry if the block entry is missing, but I'm worried about why we are missing that thing to begin with. Leveldb oddness again? Problem during conversion? Garbage collection snarfing it erroneously?
The bandaid is a bit grim, as it hides the problem rather than exposes it.
I don't disagree. Yet panicking isn't the thing to do. Returning "not found" has some minor self healing properties, if the file is there locally it will be picked up on a scan.
But by the amount of reports something is clearly screwed and I feel we should not be rolling forward.
Well I'm open for suggestions on what the underlying problem might be...
#6107 is about the right timeline too

I think may be less frequent than it looks, too. There's 70 + 53 reports of this in sentry, and given restart on panic it looks like there are probably ~10 or so reports per each device, possibly more. There are still 525 reported devices on rc.1.
We've been affected by this issue as well, on 4 separate servers, all last night after been automatically upgraded.
@couilllard45682 anything particular about those servers? Is it all of them in your setup, have they been running long, large/small dataset, odd database storage?

@calmh They're all Windows 2008R2 servers (virtualized), on a NTFS partitions. Datasets are pretty large (few hundreds of gigabytes each). What is odd that all 4 servers were used as 2 pair of 1 send only server and 1 receive only server. I had to wipe the index to get the service started (and lost most of the data on both receive only servers, is it normal?).

Receive only is special indeed, if the index is blank then there aren't supposed to be any files, so all files are local modifications and should be removed on revert. The rest is obviously not normal, no.

I think this might happen due to the methods starting here: https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/blob/master/lib/protocol/bep_extensions.go#L268

There we set `Blocks` to `nil`, but leave `BlocksHash`. So when they get written to db the blocks aren't added. Then when later querying them we see the `BlocksHash` and try to get the blocks too -> boom.

milestone.title: v1.4.0
milestone.description:
Important changes:

- A new config option maxConcurrentIncomingRequestKiB has been added to limit the maximum amount of request data being concurrently processed due to incoming requests. This limits Syncthing's peak RAM usage when there are many connected devices all requesting file data. The default is 256 MiB.

- The config option maxConcurrentScans has been removed and replaced a new config option maxFolderConcurrency. In addition to just limiting concurrent scans it now also limits concurrent sync operations. The default is the number of available CPU threads ("GOMAXPROCS").

- Syncthing now always runs the monitor process, which previously was disabled with -no-restart. This facilitates crash reporting and makes logging behave more consistently. The observed behavior with -no-restart should be the same as before but the internals differ.

- The database schema has been improved and will result in a migration plus compaction at first startup after the upgrade.

issue.body:
I unsuccessfully tried to reproduce the scenario https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/issues/6321#issuecomment-587548420. That's due to the GC not kicking in, even if noone actually has the blocks. It's enough for an ignored file to have the `BlocksHash`.

Nevertheless I believe this is a good change: It firstly makes sure that whenever `Blocks` is set to nil, so is `BlocksHash`. That means blocks can get GCed when everyone has ignored files, while it can't at the moment. I also put in a check in the db that panics if this isn't true. That could be changed to just fix it on the fly, but I'd rather know about it when it happens and fix it. And while checking for other places where the same mistake might happen, I ensured that wherever file infos are modified, that's happening through the same functions (i.e. consistently).
